name: Customer Complaint & SLA Escalation Management System

parameters.content:
## Customer Complaint & SLA Escalation Management System

### How it works

This workflow captures customer complaints from a form, validates and normalizes the submission, then creates a tracked complaint case with priority, ownership, and SLA due time. It records the case in Google Sheets, sends acknowledgement and team notifications, then waits and checks whether the complaint was resolved before the SLA threshold. If unresolved, it escalates through level 1 and potentially level 2 notifications, while resolved cases trigger a customer resolution email and closure update.

### Setup steps

- Configure the form trigger fields for customer name, customer email, complaint subject, and complaint description.
- Connect Google Sheets credentials and select the spreadsheet/table used to create, update, and retrieve complaint records.
- Connect Gmail credentials for customer acknowledgements, assigned team notifications, escalation emails, and resolution emails.
- Review the Set nodes for case ID generation, priority assignment, assigned team logic, SLA hours, and due-date calculations.
- Configure the Wait nodes to match the desired SLA check and final review intervals.

### Customization

Adjust priority rules, assigned team mapping, SLA durations, email templates, escalation recipients, and the Google Sheets schema to match the organization’s complaint management process.

## Capture and validate complaint

Receives the complaint form submission, normalizes the key customer and complaint fields, and checks whether all required fields are present.

## Prepare case details

Creates the case identifier, assigns priority and responsible team, and calculates the SLA deadline for valid complaints.

## Record and initial notifications

Creates the complaint record in Google Sheets, then branches to send the customer acknowledgement and the assigned team notification from the nearby notification nodes.

## Initial SLA status check

Waits until the first SLA review point, retrieves the complaint status from Google Sheets, and decides whether the case has already been resolved.

## Level 1 escalation

Handles the first escalation path by emailing the level 1 escalation recipient, updating the record, and waiting for the final review period.

## Post escalation review

Checks the complaint status again after the level 1 review window and branches based on whether the case remains unresolved.

## Level 2 escalation

Sends the second-level escalation email and updates the complaint record to show level 2 escalation for still-unresolved complaints.

## Resolve and close case

Sends the resolution email to the customer and marks the complaint record as closed when either status check confirms resolution.

## Invalid submission handling

Captures failed validation details by setting validation status, an error message, and a processing timestamp for incomplete submissions.
